Keywords: jvm heap, -xmx, -xms, garbage collector, gc tuning
Guidance: Leaving heap size at JVM defaults on a container lets the JVM size itself off host memory instead of the container's cgroup limit, causing OOMKilled pods even though 'heap looked fine'.
Do: Set -Xmx/-Xms explicitly (or verify -XX:+UseContainerSupport is honoring cgroup limits) and choose a GC (G1, ZGC) matched to latency/throughput needs.
Don't: Run JVM workloads in containers with default heap sizing and no verification against the container memory limit.

Keywords: threadpool, executorservice, thread starvation, connection pool exhaustion
Guidance: An unbounded or oversized thread pool (Executors.newCachedThreadPool) can spawn thousands of threads under load, exhausting memory and downstream connection pools simultaneously.
Do: Size thread pools deliberately (bounded queue + fixed pool) based on workload type (CPU-bound vs I/O-bound) and downstream capacity.
Don't: Use Executors.newCachedThreadPool() for a production service with unpredictable load.

Keywords: connection pool, hikaricp, max pool size, connection leak
Guidance: A connection pool sized larger than the database's actual max_connections causes connection errors under load; sized too small, it causes request queuing and timeouts.
Do: Size the connection pool based on (core_count * 2 + effective_spindle_count) as a starting heuristic, then tune from observed wait times, never exceeding DB max_connections / instance_count.
Don't: Set the app's connection pool max size higher than what the database server can actually accept.
Example: maximumPoolSize=10 # tuned against Postgres max_connections and instance count

Keywords: maven, gradle, dependency conflict, transitive dependency
Guidance: Conflicting transitive dependency versions ('dependency hell') silently resolve to whichever version wins the build tool's resolution strategy, which may not be the version you tested against.
Do: Explicitly declare/pin versions for dependencies known to conflict, and run dependency:tree / dependencies to audit resolution before release.
Don't: Assume transitive dependency resolution always picks a safe, tested version automatically.

Keywords: classloader leak, permgen, metaspace, hot redeploy
Guidance: Repeatedly hot-redeploying an application in a shared app server (Tomcat) without clean classloader teardown leaks Metaspace/PermGen over time until the server needs a restart.
Do: Ensure libraries don't leave static references, ThreadLocals, or shutdown hooks that pin the old classloader after redeploy; restart app servers periodically as a safety net.
Don't: Assume hot redeploys are always leak-free with no monitoring of Metaspace growth over time.

Keywords: catch exception, swallowed exception, empty catch block
Guidance: Catching a broad Exception (or Throwable) and swallowing it silently hides real failures, making production issues invisible until they cause a much bigger downstream problem.
Do: Catch the narrowest exception type meaningful to the context, log or rethrow, and never leave an empty catch block.
Don't: catch (Exception e) {} with no logging or rethrow.

Keywords: static collection, memory leak, heap growth, static map
Guidance: A static Map or List used as a cache with no eviction policy grows unbounded for the life of the JVM, eventually causing OutOfMemoryError under sustained load.
Do: Use a bounded cache (Caffeine, Guava Cache) with an eviction policy instead of a raw static collection for anything cache-like.
Don't: Use a static HashMap as an unbounded application-level cache.

Guidance: Optimizing Java code based on guesswork instead of a profiler (JFR, async-profiler) routinely targets the wrong hotspot, wasting effort on code that isn't actually the bottleneck.
Do: Profile with JDK Flight Recorder or async-profiler under representative load before optimizing anything.
Don't: Optimize suspected 'slow' code paths without first confirming them with a profiler.

Topic: Thread safety of shared mutable state
Keywords: race condition, synchronized, thread safety, concurrentmodificationexception
Guidance: Sharing a plain HashMap or ArrayList across threads without synchronization causes silent data corruption or ConcurrentModificationException under concurrent access, often only under production load.
Do: Use concurrent collections (ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList) or explicit synchronization for state shared across threads.
Don't: Share a plain HashMap across multiple threads with no synchronization.

Keywords: gc pause, stop-the-world, gc logging, latency spike
Guidance: Without GC logging enabled, a latency-sensitive service's periodic multi-hundred-millisecond stop-the-world pauses look like unexplained request spikes with no obvious cause.
Do: Enable GC logging (-Xlog:gc*) and correlate pause events with latency spikes in monitoring.
Don't: Diagnose latency spikes without ever checking whether GC pauses correlate with them.

Keywords: gradle lockfile, maven dependency lock, reproducible build
Guidance: Without dependency locking, a fresh CI build can resolve a different (newer) transitive dependency version than the one that was tested, causing 'works on my machine' build drift.
Do: Enable Gradle dependency locking (or Maven's dependency:lock-equivalent enforcer rules) so CI resolves the exact same versions every time.
Don't: Let CI re-resolve the full dependency graph fresh on every build with no lock file.

Keywords: shutdown hook, sigterm, graceful shutdown, in-flight requests
Guidance: A JVM process that doesn't handle SIGTERM gracefully drops in-flight requests immediately when Kubernetes/systemd sends the termination signal during a deploy or scale-down.
Do: Register a shutdown hook that stops accepting new work and drains in-flight requests within the orchestrator's grace period.
Don't: Let the JVM terminate immediately on SIGTERM with no drain of in-flight requests.

Keywords: heap dump, oom, memory analyzer, heapdumponoutofmemoryerror
Guidance: Restarting a service after an OutOfMemoryError with no heap dump captured throws away the exact evidence needed to find the leak, guaranteeing the same failure recurs.
Do: Enable -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError so a heap dump is captured automatically for post-mortem analysis (e.g. with Eclipse MAT).
Don't: Restart the JVM after an OOM with no heap dump captured for analysis.
